name: Places (Overture Maps, Sep 2026)
description: Pan-India points of interest from the Overture Maps Foundation release 2026-09-23.1. Names, categories (basic_category, taxonomy), addresses, websites, brands and confidence scores for shops, restaurants, ATMs, schools, hospitals, transit, monuments and more.
notes: Overture Maps Foundation places, release 2026-09-23.1, clipped to India (inside an LGD district polygon). Overture columns are kept as published except contact details (below), and `name` is a copy of names.primary added for search and simple queries. Contact emails, phone numbers and social media links are removed (personal data of sole traders). Names, addresses, sources and taxonomy stay nested in the Parquet and GeoJSON. The shapefile carries a flat subset (see columns.txt in the zip). For KML, use Filter & export on a category or area. Licences follow the source of each record (listed in `sources`): Meta, Microsoft and other contributors CDLA-Permissive-2.0, Foursquare Apache-2.0, AllThePlaces CC0-1.0.

name: Land Use & Cropping Intensity by Block (2023-24)
description: Land use and cropping intensity per LGD block in 2023-24: single, double and triple cropping, seasonal and perennial water, trees, scrub, barren and built-up land. Modelled from CoRE Stack's 10 m IndiaSAT map, not official crop statistics. Islands are not mapped and the high Himalaya only partly; mapped_pct shows coverage.
notes: Modelled data, not official crop statistics: block totals of CoRE Stack's IndiaSAT v4 land-use classification (10 m, 2023-24). Areas are in hectares and shares are of each block's mapped area, so add up hectares, not shares, when combining blocks. Not mapped: Lakshadweep and Andaman & Nicobar; partly mapped in the high Himalaya (see mapped_pct). The annual series from 2017-18 is available from CoRE Stack. Map tiles rebaked by bharatlas with the popup fields only; every column is in the parquet and the downloads.

name: Wells by District (Minor Irrigation Census 2017-18)
description: Wells per LGD district from the 6th Minor Irrigation Census (reference year 2017-18): dugwells and shallow, medium and deep tubewells, with status, pump energy source, depth and irrigation potential. Official census counts summed to districts.
source_org: Minor Irrigation (Statistics) Wing, Ministry of Jal Shakti
notes: Counts from the 6th Minor Irrigation Census (reference year 2017-18, enumerated 2019-22), Minor Irrigation (Statistics) Wing, Ministry of Jal Shakti, published on data.gov.in under GODL-India. Summed from the ground-water scheme files to LGD districts by Land Ledger; the total matches the census report (21,931,924 wells). Census districts are the 2017-18 ones: districts carved out since have no counts of their own (status new_district) and their former district keeps them (counts_pre_split); counts are not split. Irrigation potential utilised is gross, summed over seasons, not net irrigated area. Depth classes are bins of the reported scheme depth. Well locations are not published and nothing below the district is included here. Delhi, Ladakh, Lakshadweep and Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu were not in the census; Manipur and Sikkim report no ground-water schemes.

notes: Figures from the standardised income statements on CityFinance.in (Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs; run by NIUA and Janaagraha), in rupees, by National Municipal Accounts Manual line item, as published. Each polygon carries every line item for its latest year with figures (fy) and total income and expenditure for every year it has (2015-16 to 2023-24; few cities have 2017-18 or 2018-19). Tax revenue includes property tax; CityFinance does not publish it separately here. Cities are matched to Swachh Bharat Mission ULB polygons by Census 2011 town code or SBM code, never by name, and only when the states agree; each match must also be corroborated by CityFinance's own location for the city falling on (or within 2 km of) the polygon, or by the two names agreeing. Some SBM codes point at another town; a match failing both checks is left out. Both names are kept (ulbnm from SBM, cf_ulb_name from CityFinance); where they differ, SBM's label is the one that is off (e.g. Bapatla's polygon is named GUNTUR in SBM). Cities with figures but no polygon (including all of West Bengal, which SBM does not map) are not shown. CityFinance states no licence; treated here as GODL-India.

source_org: Rajya Sabha answers (MoSPI, RBI, Ministry of Finance, Income Tax Department, GSTN, MUDRA, NABARD, banks), via data.gov.in
notes: Official state-wise tables from Rajya Sabha answers, published on data.gov.in under GODL-India. Each is a one-off snapshot with its own year or date, named in every column; figures are kept as published (numbers cast to numbers, NA left empty). Money is in Rs crore unless a column says otherwise. Source state names are matched to LGD states by name with hand-checked aliases. gsdp_current_2021_22_rs_crore: GSDP at current prices (2011-12 base), Rs crore; 2021-22 is the latest year reported for nearly every state. Jammu and Kashmir is the UT figure; not compiled for Ladakh, Lakshadweep, and Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu. Source: "State/UT-wise Gross State Domestic Product (GSDP) and Percentage Growth of GSDP at Current as well as Constant (2011-12) form 2017-18 to 2022-23", Rajya Sabha session 259, unstarred question 2238, answered 20 March 2023; figures of state Directorates of Economics and Statistics as on 15-03-2023 (data.gov.in resource b94407cc-7748-41f8-b199-b2916af3228a). nsdp_per_capita_current_2021_22_rs: per capita NSDP at current prices, Rs per person (the table note says Rs crore, but the figures are rupees per person and equal the NSO per capita figures tabled in July 2024). Source: "State/UT-wise Details of Per Capita Net State Domestic Product at Current Prices from 2019-20 to 2022-23", Rajya Sabha session 262, starred question 94, answered 11 December 2023; data as on 01-08-2023 (data.gov.in resource c9bfd3c0-b9de-4a5b-8752-f72a4f2932ad). outstanding_liabilities_pct_gsdp_mar_2021_actual, outstanding_liabilities_pct_gsdp_mar_2023_be: total outstanding liabilities of the state government as percent of GSDP at end-March, 2021 actual and 2023 budget estimate (states and UTs with a legislature only). Source: "State/UT-wise Details of Total Outstanding Liabilities of States & UT with Legislature as Percent of (GSDP) from 2021 to 2023", Rajya Sabha session 260, unstarred question 1353, answered 1 August 2023; RBI, State Finances: A Study of Budgets of 2022-23 (data.gov.in resource b53abcb0-fcb2-4de9-82d5-6df1cd2a6306). gst_gross_2023_24_rs_crore: gross GST collection on domestic supplies, 2023-24 (the latest full year; the table's 2024-25 runs only to October 2024), Rs crore. Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu, reported separately, are summed. Source: "State/UT-wise Details of Gross Goods and Service Tax (GST) Collection from 2020-21 to 2024-25", Rajya Sabha session 266, unstarred question 881, answered 3 December 2024 (data.gov.in resource 5d0b81aa-d513-4dfd-9f57-84571829c049). direct_tax_gross_2022_23_rs_crore: gross direct tax collection, 2022-23, Rs crore, placed by the state code of the assessing officer's jurisdiction (so states hosting company head offices, such as Maharashtra and Delhi, carry tax earned elsewhere). Source: "State/UT-wise Details of Total Amount of Direct tax Collection during 2022-23", Rajya Sabha session 262, unstarred question 232, answered 5 December 2023 (data.gov.in resource e3b6c58c-0292-4b1b-b39a-8388a0d4a35b). mudra_loan_accounts_apr_2015_to_jan_2026, mudra_disbursed_apr_2015_to_jan_2026_rs_crore: PM Mudra Yojana loan accounts and amount disbursed, cumulative 08-04-2015 to 02-01-2026, Rs crore. Source: "State/UT-wise Details of Loan Accounts and Disbursed Amount under Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY) from 08-04-2015 to 02-01-2026", Rajya Sabha session 270, unstarred question 1199, answered 10 February 2026; provisional, as uploaded by lending institutions on the Mudra portal (data.gov.in resource 5848e4ad-2a80-4045-bae6-e705bfc05493). kcc_operative_accounts_sep_2024, kcc_outstanding_sep_2024_rs_crore: operative Kisan Credit Card accounts and amount outstanding as on 30-09-2024, Rs crore. Source: "State/UT-wise Details of Operative Kisan Credit Card (KCC) and Amount Outstanding including Maharashtra as on 30-09-2024", Rajya Sabha session 266, unstarred question 1676, answered 10 December 2024 (data.gov.in resource d7cf9477-e439-426e-9ee5-1b43dbcaabc9). pmjdy_accounts_jan_2025: PM Jan Dhan Yojana accounts as on 15-01-2025. Source: "State/UT-wise Number of PMJDY accounts, PMJJBY, PMSBY, and APY Enrolments under National Mission for Financial Inclusion (NMFI) during 31-12-2024 and 15-01-2025", Rajya Sabha session 267, unstarred question 220, answered 4 February 2025; source: banks (data.gov.in resource 996d63c6-4759-4b12-90b4-b6ce61d337e3). Rows skipped on purpose: gsdp: the erstwhile state of Jammu and Kashmir including Ladakh (figures to 2018-19 only); the UT row is used. Source rows with no LGD state: gst: Other Territory; gst: Centre Jurisdiction; direct_tax: N/A.

name: Railway stations
description: One point per Indian Railways station or halt, with its station code, merged by bharatlas from two government copies of the CRIS station layer (PM GatiShakti and the IR GIS portal) and Wikidata station codes, with a source and match-confidence column on every row.
source_org: Indian Railways (CRIS), via PM GatiShakti and the IR GIS portal; Wikidata
notes: Merged by bharatlas and published under CC BY 4.0 (credit: bharatlas, Indian Railways / CRIS, PM GatiShakti, Wikidata). Sources: (1) PM GatiShakti railway stations (BISAG-N), drawn from CRIS's Indian Railways station layer; (2) the Indian Railways GIS portal stations (irgeoportal.gov.in, CRIS), the ir_stations layer; both compiled by ramSeraph/indianopenmaps (DataMeet community, CC0 1.0) and republished with credit under bharatlas.com/about#sources-and-licensing; (3) Wikidata items with an Indian Railways station code (P5696), CC0 1.0. Every location comes from CRIS. CRIS records most stations as several points (start, centre, end, platforms); points sharing a station code become one row at their medoid, and uncoded points within 1 km fold into it (source_points counts them, source_spread_m is how far they spread). Points of one code more than 2 km apart are treated as different stations. GatiShakti is used first; the IR portal adds the 52 codes GatiShakti lacks. A Wikidata code missing from CRIS is placed on the nearest CRIS station within 1.5 km whose name or description agrees (match_method name+distance; this also links CRIS's older codes to the current ones, e.g. CSTM/CSMT, BCT/MMCT, HNZM/NZM, KEU/KIUL: stn_code keeps CRIS's code, code holds Wikidata's), or on an uncoded CRIS point within 500 m on distance alone (distance). match_confidence: high = CRIS code and Wikidata agree within 1 km; medium = CRIS code not in Wikidata or 1 to 2 km away, or a name-confirmed match; low = Wikidata more than 2 km away, a distance-only match, or an uncoded CRIS point (stn_code empty). Checked against OpenStreetMap: high rows sit a median 26 m from OSM's station with the same code (98% within 500 m), medium 90%, low 87%. OpenStreetMap is used only for that check and is not merged, because its ODbL licence would require the whole layer to stay under ODbL. Every source column is kept as published (sttncode, sttnname, fdetail ... from CRIS; item, code, coord, label from Wikidata; coord is Wikidata's point, kept for reference, never the location), except the CRIS GIS accounts that created and last edited each point (created_us, last_edite), left out because some are individuals' usernames. Known gaps: about 800 Wikidata codes have no CRIS point to sit on and are left out (e.g. Kalyan KYN, whose only CRIS point is coded THK, and Lokmanya Tilak Terminus LTT); Wikidata positions are mostly copied from the 2016 datameet/railways compilation and sit a median ~90 m and a 90th percentile ~1.2 km from CRIS, so they are not used as locations. About 300 rows are uncoded, unnamed CRIS points. CRIS state names are as published (mixed case, some blank).

name: Water Bodies (1st Census, 2017-18)
description: Ponds, tanks, lakes, reservoirs and check dams from the 1st Census of Water Bodies (reference year 2017-18): one point per water body with its type, ownership, use, storage, water spread, encroachment and repair or revival schemes.
source_org: Minor Irrigation (Statistics) Wing, Ministry of Jal Shakti
notes: Incomplete: this layer holds 1,101,912 of the 2,424,540 water bodies the 1st Census of Water Bodies counted, because its source, the data.gov.in API of the 1st Water Bodies Census, holds fewer for some States. Partial States: Andhra Pradesh 21,052 of 190,777; Assam 72,119 of 172,492; Odisha 61,802 of 181,837; Uttar Pradesh 41,435 of 245,087; West Bengal 54,876 of 747,480. Tripura is missing (the census counted 36,239 there). The data is complete for the other 27 States/UTs. 82,338 records without usable coordinates are kept with no geometry (no point on the map). 1st Census of Water Bodies (reference year 2017-18), Department of Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation and the Minor Irrigation (Statistics) Wing, Ministry of Jal Shakti, published per State/UT on data.gov.in under GODL-India and read through its API. Columns are as published ("NA" or "NULL" in a numeric column becomes empty); unique_id holds the census's own state/district/block/village codes, not LGD codes. The point is the enumerator's latitude_dec/longitude_dec as published (the manual asks for the north-west corner of the water body); many were keyed in by hand and some are stacked on one spot. Of 1,101,912 records: 1,019,233 fall inside India's bounding box, 341 outside it, 0 at (0,0), 25 have impossible values (beyond 180 degrees longitude or 90 latitude) and 82,313 have no numeric coordinates (32 of them give degrees/minutes/seconds text such as 17/41/29). A registry, not satellite mapping: compare with wris_waterbodies, do not treat them as the same features.
